issue.title: Hourly backup discards a completed rotation when rsync returns the benign exit 24

task_type_fields.impact:
## Impact

Roughly two thirds of hourly `/home` backups are thrown away, so the newest rotation is
routinely hours stale and the recovery point is much worse than the hourly schedule implies.

It also directly gates epic bob-cli-15's `/mnt/hercules` steady-state goal. That epic's
two structural fixes — the `bryan/**/target/` + `bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/`
excludes (bob-cli-15.5) and `--link-dest` hardlink rotations (bob-cli-15.6) — only reclaim
space *as rotations cycle*. Eleven `/home` rotations still hold a full
`bryan/projects/github/sase-org/sase-core/target` copy (the audit measured one at 120G);
they age out only when their tier rotates. Every discarded run postpones the array's
drop from 95% used toward the epic's 80% target.

This defect predates epic bob-cli-15 (failures appear in `/var/mail/root` well before the
epic started on 2026-08-26 08:19 EDT). Filed by the bob-cli-15 land agent.
task_type_fields.location: `_backup()` rsync error handling in `/home/bryan/Sync/bin/cron.jobs/backup.sh` (the `if _run_rsync ... ; then ... else BACKUP_ERROR=$((BACKUP_ERROR | RSYNC_ERROR))` branch)
task_type_fields.repro:
## Repro

```bash
sudo grep -c 'hourly_backup exited with return code 16' /var/mail/root   # -> 1931
```

`_backup()` treats any non-zero rsync exit as fatal. rsync exit **24** is not a failure —
it means "some files vanished before they could be transferred", which happens on every
run because `/home/bryan/.sase/axe/lumberjacks/**/runs/*` and
`/home/bryan/.sase/agents_sync/cache/staging/*` are short-lived agent scratch files.

On exit 24 the script discards the freshly-completed rotation (`rm -rf "${_to}"`), skips
the atomic `mv` chain, and returns — so the rotation never advances even though rsync
copied everything that still existed.

Sample failure rate from `/var/mail/root` (only failures generate mail):

| Date       | Failed hourly runs |
| ---------- | ------------------ |
| Aug 24     | 13                 |
| Aug 25     | 20                 |
| Aug 26 (to 10:00) | 6           |

On 2026-08-26 only three hourly rotations landed (00:39, 05:39, 07:56) against six
failures. `/mnt/hercules/backup/home/hourly` was still stamped 07:56 at 10:15.

Fix: treat 24 (and arguably 23) as success, or at most as a warning that still commits
the rotation, while keeping genuine errors fatal. `--delete-excluded` is active, so a
committed rotation is still correct.

evidence.note: Routed by bob-cli-an.land from bob-cli-an.2 PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #6. Reproduced after the hardened root chain (bob-cli-96) landed: the gated 2026-10-22 exercise returned BACKUP exit 16 from rsync code 24 on short-lived ~/.sase scratch plus an rm staging race; restore sample still matched. On 2026-10-23 at 12:25 EDT the newest /mnt/hercules/backup/home/hourly rotation was 04:24, with hourly-2..4 at 01:24, 23:24, and 20:24. Rotations land only about every third hourly run, as in the original August evidence. The TOO_SOON guard is only 30 min, so the gaps are discarded rotations. Daily (last 2026-10-18), weekly (last 2026-09-26), and monthly (last 2026-04-23) rotations are also stale. Their cause is not verified without root mail, but they use the same discard-on-any-rsync-error logic. The root-executed copy now lives at /usr/local/lib/athena-cron/backup.sh, installed from tailnet hosts/athena/root-cron/lib/backup.sh via install_root_cron.py, so the fix must go there through a reviewed sudo install, not into ~/db/bin. Epic plan bob-cli-an kept exit-24 policy out of its own scope only.
